explanation: Recursively permute the suffix, then insert the removed first character at every position of each smaller permutation. A set removes duplicate strings.
correctness: Every permutation has some position occupied by the removed character; deleting it yields a suffix permutation generated recursively. Reinserting at all positions therefore covers every result, and the set prevents duplicates.
walkthrough: For ab, recurse on b to obtain the set {b}. Insert a before b and after b, yielding {ab,ba}. The base case for an empty suffix is the singleton set containing the empty string, which makes the first insertion possible. Return a set of strings; the adapter displays a JSON array and compares membership without imposing output order.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
Empty input returns the singleton set {""}; repeated characters yield distinct strings only, not repeated output entries.
timeComplexity: Expected O(n*n!) worst-case time: with distinct characters there are n! output strings, each constructed/hashed in O(n); all smaller recursion levels are dominated by this bound.
spaceComplexity: O(n*n!) worst-case result and intermediate string storage, plus recursion depth O(n); repeated characters can reduce the number of distinct results.
